sonnet.problem: The true/false statement makes two claims: the nations are terrified, and the LORD tells Israel to be terrified too. The first is true and the second is false, so it is not a single test.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: Verse 6 does not say who is speaking. The cards name 'the prophet' as the speaker here and on later cards (stop 1 cards 12-14, stop 2 cards 1, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14), and the passage never names him as the speaker of verses 6-16.
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: This choice card tests verse 7 before any story card has told it, and the statement itself hands over the verse's content, so there is nothing to reason out. Story card 13 then tells verse 7 afterward. The statement also bundles in a background claim about the LORD telling Israel not to fear the idols.
sonnet.rule: Cards follow the passage in order. A choice card can look back at a verse an earlier card in the same stop told, but never jumps ahead.

sonnet.problem: Verse 12 has not been told on any story card. The true/false statement restates the whole verse, so the baker can only guess or simply accept it, with no way to reason to the answer.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.
